newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia minister replaces disgraced state chief.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia minister replaces disgraced state chief.

text.p: Malaysia on Friday named veteran cabinet minister Abu Hassan Omar to replace Selangor state's chief minister who quit last month after he was charged with trying to smuggle nearly US$1 million out of Australia.

At a news conference, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that Abu Hassan, 56, minister of domestic trade and consumer affairs, would replace Muhammad Muhammad Taib as head of central Selangor state.
Anwar made the announcement following a meeting on Friday with the Sultan of Selangor.
"I have met this morning (with the Sultan) and forwarded the name fixed by the prime minister, that is Datuk Abu Hassan Omar," Anwar said.
Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad in on an African tour.

Muhammad Taib, a vice-president of Malaysia's dominant political party, the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), was detained at Brisbane International Airport last December after the equivalent of US$940,000 was found in his luggage.
He was later charged with failing to declare to customs an amount over A$5,000 and making a false declaration. His trial has been fixed for August 19.
Muhammad Taib resigned as chief minister but said he was not quitting his UMNO party post.
